text: What is the primary objective of preparing a Trial Balance?
options: To prepare the Balance Sheet
To prepare the Income Statement
To verify the arithmetical accuracy of the ledger accounts
To prepare the Cash Flow Statement
correctAnswer: To verify the arithmetical accuracy of the ledger accounts
explanation: The primary objective of preparing a Trial Balance is to verify the arithmetical accuracy of the ledger accounts. It is a list of all general ledger accounts and their balances, which helps to ensure that the debits and credits are equal and that there are no mathematical errors in the ledger accounts.

chapter: Ch 6: Trial Balance and Rectification of Errors

text: Which of the following errors will not affect the Trial Balance?
options: Error of Omission
Error of Commission
Error of Principle
All of the above
explanation: Errors of omission, commission, and principle are all types of errors that do not affect the Trial Balance. An error of omission occurs when a transaction is not recorded at all, an error of commission occurs when a transaction is recorded in the wrong account, and an error of principle occurs when a transaction is recorded using the wrong accounting principle.

text: What is a Suspense Account?
options: A temporary account used to balance the Trial Balance
A permanent account used to record assets
A temporary account used to record liabilities
A permanent account used to record equity
correctAnswer: A temporary account used to balance the Trial Balance
explanation: A Suspense Account is a temporary account used to balance the Trial Balance when there are errors or discrepancies that cannot be immediately identified or corrected. It is used to ensure that the debits and credits are equal, and it is closed once the errors are identified and corrected.

text: How are errors of omission rectified?
options: By passing a rectification entry
By preparing a new Trial Balance
By preparing a new Balance Sheet
By preparing a new Income Statement
explanation: Errors of omission are rectified by passing a rectification entry, which involves recording the omitted transaction in the correct account. For example, if a purchase of goods is not recorded, a rectification entry would be passed to debit the Purchases account and credit the Cash account.

text: Which of the following is an example of an error of principle?
options: Recording a purchase of goods as a sale
Recording a sale of goods as a purchase
Recording a salary expense as a capital expenditure
Recording a capital expenditure as a revenue expenditure
correctAnswer: Recording a salary expense as a capital expenditure
explanation: An error of principle occurs when a transaction is recorded using the wrong accounting principle. For example, recording a salary expense as a capital expenditure is an error of principle, as salary expenses should be recorded as expenses, not as capital expenditures.

text: Which of the following is an example of a compensating error?
options: An error of omission and an error of commission
An error of principle and an error of omission
An error of commission and an error of principle
An error of omission and an error of principle
correctAnswer: An error of commission and an error of principle
explanation: A compensating error occurs when two or more errors cancel each other out, resulting in a correct Trial Balance. For example, if a sale of goods is recorded as a purchase (an error of commission) and a purchase of goods is recorded as a sale (an error of principle), the two errors will cancel each other out, resulting in a correct Trial Balance.
